subject.title: [Bug]: macOS app 'Launch at login' stops sticking / appears to turn itself off after app updates

question: Should the macOS app persist OpenClaw-owned Launch at login intent and re-register the app LaunchAgent after update/startup drift, or should live launchd/System Settings state remain authoritative?
rationale: Current code treats live launchd state as the toggle source of truth, while the report asks for enabled intent to survive app replacement/update; choosing the repair path affects user control and upgrade semantics.

options.title: Persist intent and reconcile drift
options.body: Store explicit in-app enabled intent and re-register only the app-owned LaunchAgent after update/startup drift, with guards for deliberate external disablement.

options.title: Keep launchd authoritative
options.body: Leave live launchd/System Settings state as the source of truth and update UI/docs so OpenClaw does not restore externally disabled login items.

options.title: Wait for packaged update proof
options.body: Keep this parked until a current-main Sparkle update repro shows exactly which state flips before selecting repair behavior.

recommendation.title: Persist intent and reconcile drift
recommendation.body: Store explicit in-app enabled intent and re-register only the app-owned LaunchAgent after update/startup drift, with guards for deliberate external disablement.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history on the launchd-backed checkbox and LaunchAgent manager ownership path.
